extracted.intended_audience: Title IX Coordinators, K-12 and postsecondary institution administrators, institutional legal counsel, and policymakers implementing Part 106 Title IX regulations
extracted.subtask_short: Title IX complaint and grievance rules
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards and definitions governing reporting, filing formal complaints, parties (complainant/respondent), supportive measures, and the scope of actionable sexual harassment under the Department's final Title IX regulations (34 CFR Part 106).

rubrics_metrics.name: Parental/guardian authority to act on behalf of student
rubrics_metrics.description: The extent to which a recipient must abide by the wishes of a parent depends on the scope of the parent's legal right to act on the student's behalf; final regulations add §106.6(g) to acknowledge parents/guardians' legal rights to act for a complainant, respondent, or other individual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title IX Coordinators may assist parents or guardians in acting on behalf of a student, but must respect legal limits of parental authority and the student's own wishes where applicable. Assistance must not be used to pressure the complainant (or parent) to file a formal complaint rather than to provide administrative help consistent with the individual's intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on intimidation, threats, and coercion (retaliation protection)
rubrics_metrics.description: No person may intimidate, threaten, or coerce any person for the purpose of interfering with a person's rights under Title IX, including the right not to participate in a grievance process; final regulations add §106.71 prohibiting retaliation and protecting the right to participate or not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must ensure processes and staff actions do not chill participation or non-participation. Protections for non-participation are explicit and must be communicated and enforced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted methods for filing a formal complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: A formal complaint may be filed with the Title IX Coordinator in person, by mail, by electronic mail, and by any additional method designated by the recipient; a formal complaint must be a written document or electronic submission (telephone alone is not sufficient).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic submissions (e.g., email or online portals) are authorized; a formal complaint must contain the complainant's physical or digital signature or otherwise indicate that the complainant is the person filing. Recipients may designate online portals or other electronic systems as additional acceptable filing methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator contact information and prominence
rubrics_metrics.description: The contact information required to be listed for the Title IX Coordinator under §106.8(a) must be prominently displayed on the recipient's website (if the recipient has a website) and in any of the recipient's handbooks or catalogs (§106.8(b) revised).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prominent listing is intended to make reporting and filing as accessible as possible; recipients should ensure accuracy and visibility of Coordinator contact methods across institutional materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator may assist in preparing a formal complaint (without coercion)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Title IX Coordinator may assist a complainant (or parent) in filling out a document intended to serve as a formal complaint but must take care not to pressure the complainant (or parent) to file a formal complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a coordinator helps prepare a filing, the final submitted document still must contain the complainant's physical or digital signature or otherwise indicate the complainant is the filer. Assistance may include writing down a verbal report for signature or facilitating electronic submission, provided the complainant's assent is clear and not coerced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms and methods of notice (reporting) to Title IX Coordinator are unrestricted
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulations do not restrict the form in which notice (e.g., a report of alleged sexual harassment) is given to the Title IX Coordinator, an official with authority, or an elementary/secondary school employee; notice may be given by in person, mail, telephone, email, or other means.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting (giving notice) is distinct from filing a formal complaint. Recipients must accept notice through the contact methods listed for the Title IX Coordinator; reporting should trigger recipient response obligations even if a formal complaint is not filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients must offer prompt individualized supportive measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must promptly implement individualized services designed to restore or preserve the complainant's equal access to education, regardless of whether a formal complaint is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supportive measures should be available once notice is received; they are not contingent on filing a formal complaint. Examples and tailoring of measures are provided elsewhere in the regulations and preamble; recipients should act promptly to preserve access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complainant must be participating or attempting to participate at time of filing
rubrics_metrics.description: To trigger the obligation to investigate via a formal complaint, the complainant must be participating in, or attempting to participate in, the recipient's education program or activity at the time of filing a formal complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ‘Attempting to participate’ includes graduated individuals seeking admission to another program, those on leave of absence intending to return, alumni involved in alumni programs, or individuals who left due to harassment but wish to re-enroll. This preserves access to remedies for persons with ongoing or prospective educational involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal complaint may allege harassment against an unidentified respondent; limits on sanctions
rubrics_metrics.description: The §106.30 definition states a formal complaint is a document alleging sexual harassment 'against a respondent,' but a complainant need not identify the respondent; however, a recipient cannot impose disciplinary sanctions without complying with §106.45 (which requires sending written notice of allegations and identities of parties if known).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the complainant refuses or cannot identify a respondent, the recipient still must promptly offer supportive measures and may investigate to identify a respondent; disciplinary sanctions are not permitted until grievance process requirements (including notice) can be met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance process required before imposing disciplinary sanctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 106.44(a) and §106.45 require that recipients follow a grievance process that complies with §106.45 prior to imposing disciplinary sanctions on a respondent; §106.45(b)(2) requires sending written notice of allegations, including party identities if known, 'upon receipt of a formal complaint.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must ensure procedural steps (notice, opportunity to respond, investigation, adjudication per §106.45) are followed before sanctioning. Failure to follow the grievance process precludes imposition of discipline under Title IX for those allegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and scope of 'postsecondary institution'
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department revised §106.30 to define 'postsecondary institution' (used in §§106.44 and 106.45) by reference to §106.2(l)-(o) (graduate, undergraduate, professional, and vocational education institutions) and replaced 'institutions of higher education' with 'postsecondary institutions' throughout the regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarifies that the Title IX regulations are promulgated under Title IX (not HEA Title IV definitions) and limits the application of the 'postsecondary institution' term to the specified sections. Institutions should consult §106.2 for the precise statutory/regulatory definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'respondent' (who may be a respondent)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'respondent' is an 'individual'—which may include a student, faculty member, or other employee of the recipient, or an unaffiliated person; the Department intentionally does not limit 'respondent' to individuals against whom a formal complaint has been filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term 'respondent' is used neutrally and consistently across the regulations; recipients' general response obligations under §106.44(a) can affect persons alleged to have committed sexual harassment even where no formal grievance is filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-pronged definition of actionable sexual harassment
rubrics_metrics.description: The §106.30 definition adopts a three-part formulation: (1) quid pro quo harassment by any recipient employee; (2) unwelcome conduct on the basis of sex that is so severe, pervasive, and objectively offensive that it effectively denies a person equal access to education (the Davis standard); and (3) sexual assault and the Clery Act/VAWA offenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quid pro quo harassment and the enumerated Clery Act/VAWA sex offenses are treated as per se actionable sexual harassment (do not require showing of severity/pervasiveness). The Davis 'catch-all' for verbal/expressive harassment requires severity, pervasiveness, and objective offensiveness to avoid First Amendment concerns. Recipients may treat other misconduct more broadly in their own codes, but Title IX enforcement is limited to these categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrow tailoring to protect free speech and academic freedom
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulations limit the definition of actionable harassment (especially for speech/expressive conduct) to avoid chilling constitutionally protected speech and to respect academic freedom; specifically, purely verbal conduct is actionable under the Davis standard only when severe, pervasive, and objectively offensive such that it denies equal access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must take care not to interpret or apply harassment standards so broadly that protected speech is suppressed; the Department emphasizes consistency with Supreme Court precedent and recognizes differences between educational settings and workplace Title VII standards. Non-punitive institutional responses (supportive measures, programming, institutional speech) remain available for conduct that does not meet the Title IX standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients retain discretion to address broader misconduct outside Title IX enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Although Title IX actionable harassment is defined narrowly, recipients retain discretion to use their own, broader definitions of misconduct for institutional codes and to respond in non-punitive ways (supportive measures, institutional speech, programming) to conduct that does not meet Title IX's definition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department notes recipients may adopt broader policies for campus conduct but Title IX obligations (investigation, grievance process, sanctions) are only triggered when the conduct falls within the §106.30 definition. Recipients should clearly distinguish between Title IX processes and other institutional responses.
